title: Shake That Tree, Darlene
subject: an old Texas couple bringing in their pecan harvest in November with a tree shaker borrowed from the co-op for one afternoon only, the husband clamping the trunk while his wife drives the sweeper, nuts bouncing off the truck roof, both racing the co-op man who is coming at four to take the shaker back
caption: Western swing, Texas dancehall revival in the Bob Wills line. Twin fiddles playing harmonized swing lines, a swinging lap steel guitar taking hot breaks, upright slap bass, boom-chick acoustic rhythm guitar, rolling barrelhouse piano and a brushed snare shuffle. Live-room dancehall sound, warm ribbon-mic tone, light room reverb, the whole band playing at once. Male baritone with an easy Texas drawl, band members hollering between lines. 168 BPM, C major. Rowdy, sunny and teasing. No modern pop drums, no autotune, no trap, no rock electric guitar, no stadium country production.
lyrics:
[Intro - twin fiddles and steel kick off, band holler]

[Verse 1]
The co-op gave us one afternoon
One big yellow shaker and a man named June
Said I'll be back at four o'clock sharp
Don't you go shaking my good sense apart

[Pre-Chorus]
I clamp the trunk and I give her the nod
Darlene's on the sweeper hollering at God

[Chorus]
Shake that tree, Darlene
The pecans are coming down on the roof of the old machine
They're bouncing off the truck and the dog and me
Shake that tree, Darlene, shake that tree

[Verse 2]
Forty-one trees that my daddy put in
Half of them crooked and the rest too thin
The sweeper's choking on a bushel of leaves
She's kicking it and cussing with her rolled-up sleeves

[Pre-Chorus]
It's a quarter to three and we're on tree nine
She says honey, are you counting or wasting time

[Chorus]
Shake that tree, Darlene
The pecans are coming down on the hat I bought in Abilene
They're bouncing off the truck and the dog and me
Shake that tree, Darlene, shake that tree

[Instrumental Break - steel guitar then fiddles]

[Bridge - piano and slap bass]
Four o'clock and here comes June
Darlene hands him pie on a paper spoon

[Chorus]
Shake that tree, Darlene
June's on the shaker now, the slickest I have seen
They're bouncing off the truck and the dog and me
Shake that tree, Darlene, one more tree

[Outro - twin fiddle tag, band holler, final hit]
